chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from Abdullah ibn Suleyman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He said to me: 'Our secret has not ceased to be concealed until it came to be in the hands of the children of Kaysan, so they began to narrate it in the roads and the towns of the black land (Iraq).'

key_terms.السَّوَادِ: The black land (referring to the fertile region of Iraq, particularly around Baghdad)
key_terms.سِرُّنَا: Our secret (referring to the Imams' hidden knowledge or authority)
key_terms.وُلْدِ كَيْسَانَ: Children of Kaysan (a specific lineage or group known for transmitting Ahl al-Bayt traditions)

ai.seo_question: Who revealed the secret of the Imams and how did it become public?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reveals that the esoteric knowledge (Sirr) of the Imams remained concealed until it was entrusted to the children of Kaysan, whose public dissemination in the roads and towns of Iraq marked a pivotal shift in the visibility of Imamate authority. This narration highlights the historical transition from the era of minor concealment (al-Ghaybah al-Sughra) to the broader public awareness of the Imam's lineage, underscoring the gradual unfolding of divine secrets within the Shia community.
